fact: Tech Africa News reports the Ministry of Digital Transition completed phase one of the PNCR in August 2024 and launched phases two (18 billion CFA, 240 localities) and three (10 billion CFA, 160 localities), within a 38 billion CFA programme to connect 575 rural localities.
ANSUT's Honoré Aka said the rural connectivity emergency programme launched in 2025 connected 500 villages to digital infrastructure and connectivity services.
ANSUT's Honoré Aka said 300 new localities are to be added to the rural digital connectivity effort in 2026.
We Are Tech Africa reports the Ministry of Digital Transition is leading PNCR phase II through 25 September 2025 to connect 30 additional localities to high-speed internet.
We Are Tech Africa reports the villages of Yanfissa, Kangana, Kognimansso and Dougbe in Worodougou are already online under PNCR phase II.
Citing ITU DataHub, the article gives internet penetration of 52.7% in urban areas against 24.6% in rural areas.
Fraternité Matin reports ANSUT said that under the PNCR, run by the Ministry of Digital Transition, 575 additional rural localities will be connected by end October 2025.

ANSUT's director general told the minister on 11 February 2026 that the agency is moving a growing number of villages out of digital isolation as part of Côte d'Ivoire's universal service policy, with no number given.

The government's National Rural Connectivity Program (PNCR) aims to reach 575 rural localities and about 825,675 residents by December 2025, with a second phase from 1 August adding 16 villages, and to continue into 2026, per the Ministry of Digital Transition.
Under the PNCR, seven rural localities across several regions were reported connected, with radio sites activated from 15 July 2025.
The national rural connectivity programme, led by minister Kalil Konaté, aims to cover about 500 localities in the short term, per Digital Mag reporting on the SUTEL 2024 workshop.

A government communique of 2026-08-24 says Cote d'Ivoire is continuing its FCFA 38 billion Programme national de connectivite rurale to bring mobile network and internet access to 575 localities, with phase two (FCFA 18 billion, 240 localities) and phase three (FCFA 10 billion, 160 localities) following.
The government says phase one of the PNCR, completed in 2024, built 160 radio sites in 175 localities, benefiting about 221,267 inhabitants.
ANSUT's director general said on 2026-08-11 that the universal service agency is working to connect 300 localities to reach 300,000 inhabitants, citing that 70% of rural households have no internet.
CIPESA says ANSUT's universal access efforts include broadband connectivity for rural communities.
